#405 fix r3.summary:
I amended the #405 commit. It is still one commit on 8f7d98aa: it was e55a9fc8 and is now d49f51f0. I did not push it. Before fixing anything I reproduced each item on e55a9fc8 (r3/repro-red-e55a9fc8.txt).
(1) Whitespace. I removed the refusal. In its place, CatalogSpec.__new__ strips a package, URL or git spelling once, so the resolver, resolve_entry_source, update's wrap and a Python caller all produce the same stripped string, and every check and the installer read that string. A path spelling keeps its exact string, and _names_no_cwd judges that exact string. So ' /abs/x.whl' counts as relative and is refused, and the message says the leading space makes it relative; '/abs/x.whl ' is that exact name. spelled_as_path reads the shape from the stripped string. No whitespace refusal remains, and no case needed one. A git record written with a trailing space now updates.
(2) The typed update filter is no longer stripped, and _install_spec(..., 'path') resolves it, the same function a typed install uses. New rows kill mutants S14 and S28.
(3) Order of checks: after the 'starts like a path' test, a string that parses as a requirement with a version specifier, a marker or a URL is a package or URL. A bare token ending in an archive suffix stays a path spelling, including one with [extras]. I pinned rows for all six listed spellings and four more.
(4) The origin check already ran for every CatalogSpec. New rows pin it for build_pip_args and verify_and_pin when the caller's kind agrees, and they kill Codex's mutant.
(5) source remove has no way to target one record exactly, so the message now says plainly that it matches by spec or name and will also drop a package record of the same name. A row and a live run confirm what the message says.
CHANGELOG, ADR-0255 (Status line, sweep table, known limits, a new 'Review round 3' part), the ADR index row and both guide copies changed with the code. The commit message has a REVIEW ROUND 3 section. Kit: /Users/handochan/dev/aelix-ai/.omc/probes/405-live/r3/

sweep: Every CatalogSpec construction site is normalised by __new__: resolve_entry_target (3 sites), resolve_entry_source, _upgrade_and_report, and Python callers. Path spellings are kept exact.
_origin_spec_problem: the whitespace branch is removed. The relative-path test reads the exact string, and the message adds a note when a leading space is what makes a path relative.

owner_decisions: I deviated from the rule as written: [extras] alone does not make a string a package. With the pip backend, 'x==1.0+v.whl' fails: pip reads it as a filename in aelix's installer directory, as on 8f7d98aa. uv installs it. Should aelix rewrite that spelling for pip, or leave it as a documented limit?

nonblocking.title: source remove advice understates what it drops: it also matches by cwd-resolved path
nonblocking.detail: _remove_source also resolves the target against the CURRENT directory (_source_identity(target,'path')). The printed `aelix extension source remove -- local-ext` therefore also drops an ABSOLUTE path record <cwd>/local-ext, whose spec and name are both something other than 'local-ext'. The message says it drops any other source or record whose spec or name is 'local-ext'. The guide says 'whose spec or name is the same string'. Both are true but incomplete, and the behaviour is pre-existing. Suggested fix: add 'or whose path, read from this directory, is <cwd>/<spec>', or advise running the command from another directory.
